lessons.title: Choosing Shipping Carriers and Services
lessons.body: Choosing the right shipping carrier is critical to your reselling profit. In Africa, options vary by country. In Nigeria, use GIG Logistics, Kwik Delivery, or Sendbox for local deliveries. In Kenya, pick Pickup Mtaani, Sendy, or G4S. In South Africa, The Courier Guy, PostNet, and Pargo are reliable. For international shipping, DHL, FedEx, and UPS are common but expensive. Always compare rates: a 1kg package from Lagos to Accra via DHL costs about $50, while local courier GIG charges around â¦3,000 ($4) for same-city delivery. For small items, use registered mail through your national postal serviceâitâs cheaper but slower. Consider speed: customers expect delivery within 2-5 days locally. Offer standard (3-5 days) and express (1-2 days) options. Track everything: use carriers with online tracking and SMS updates. Negotiate rates once you ship over 20 packages per month. Also, check insurance: for high-value items, pay extra 1-2% of item value. Test carriers with a few shipments before committing. Ask other resellers in Facebook groups like âJumia Sellersâ or âTakealot Resellersâ for recommendations. Always keep receipts and tracking numbers. Avoid cash-on-delivery unless you trust the carrier; many lose money on returns. Remember, reliable shipping builds repeat customers.

lessons.title: Calculating Shipping Costs and Labels
lessons.body: To price shipping, you need three numbers: weight, dimensions, and destination. Use a digital scale (â¦5,000 on Jumia) and a tape measure. For local shipping in Nigeria, most couriers charge by weight: first 1kg costs â¦1,500-â¦2,500, each additional kg â¦500. Volumetric weight applies for bulky items: (length x width x height in cm) / 5000. For example, a box 30x20x10cm = 6000/5000 = 1.2kg, so you pay for 2kg. Always round up. For international, DHL charges about $30 for 0.5kg to UK. Use online calculators: DHL Express, FedEx, or local courier websites. Create labels using free tools: Sendbox, ShipStation, or even Google Docs with a barcode. Include: sender address, receiver address, phone numbers, tracking number, and weight. Print on adhesive paper or tape a paper label securely. For FBA, you must use Amazonâs Partner Carrier or approved couriers and print FBA labels from Seller Central. Never guess costsâundercharging eats your profit. Add 10% buffer for fuel surcharges and remote area fees. For returns, pre-print return labels and include them in the package. Keep a shipping log in Excel: date, order ID, carrier, cost, tracking. Review monthly to spot overcharges. Many resellers lose money by not weighing accurately. Buy a scale today.

lessons.title: Packaging Best Practices for Safe Delivery
lessons.body: Packaging protects your product and your reputation. In Africa, rough handling is common, so over-pack. Use double-walled cardboard boxes for fragile items. For electronics, wrap in bubble wrap (â¦2,000 per roll) and use foam peanuts or shredded paper. For clothing, use poly mailers (â¦500 for 50)âtheyâre waterproof and cheap. For liquids, seal in a ziplock bag, then wrap in bubble wrap, and mark âThis Side Upâ. Use strong tape: packing tape (â¦1,000 per roll) not cellotape. For international shipping, customs may open packages, so include a packing slip inside with item description and value. Never use old newspapers as paddingâthey get soggy and ink rubs off. For FBA, follow Amazonâs strict rules: no loose items, poly bag items smaller than 5cm, and suffocation warning labels. Use a thermal label printer (â¦50,000) for professional labels. For local deliveries, use courier-provided bags if available. Test your packaging: drop the box from waist heightâif it survives, good. Add âFragileâ stickers. For high-value items, use tamper-evident bags. Keep packaging costs low: buy in bulk from Alibaba or local suppliers like Packaging Nigeria. Reuse boxes from your own online orders. Always include a thank-you card and return instructions. Good packaging reduces damage claims and returns, saving you money and stress.

lessons.title: Using Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA)
lessons.body: FBA lets you store products in Amazon warehouses; they pick, pack, and ship for you. This is powerful for African resellers selling to the US, UK, or Germany. But it has strict rules. First, you need an Amazon Seller Central account (professional plan $39.99/month). Create a shipment plan: choose products, print FBA labels (using thermal printer), and box them. Each box must have an FBA box ID label. Ship via Amazonâs partnered carriers (DHL, UPS) or use a freight forwarder like Shipbymail or MyUS. From Nigeria, shipping 10kg to Amazon US costs about $150 via DHL. Amazon charges fulfillment fees: for a 1kg standard-size item, about $5.50. Storage fees: $0.75 per cubic foot per month (Jan-Sep) and higher in Q4. You must comply with expiration dates, safety, and labeling. For African sellers, the biggest challenge is customs and import duties. Use a freight forwarder who handles customs. Also, you must have a US tax ID (EIN) or use Amazonâs tax calculation service. FBA can boost sales with Prime badge, but only if you manage inventory well. Avoid long-term storage fees: keep 2-3 months of stock. Use Amazonâs inventory performance index (IPI) to monitor. If you sell in Europe, you need VAT registration. Start small: test with 20-30 units. Many Africans succeed with FBA by selling African prints, shea butter, or crafts. But calculate all fees before committing.

lessons.title: International Shipping and Customs
lessons.body: International shipping from Africa is expensive and paperwork-heavy. You need a commercial invoice, packing list, and customs declaration. For each shipment, declare the correct valueâunder-declaring is illegal and can lead to seizure. Use HS codes (Harmonized System) for your products. For example, shea butter HS code 1515.90. Customs duties vary: US charges 0-10% depending on item; EU charges 0-17% plus VAT (20% in UK). African exporters can use AGOA (US) or EU-ACP agreements for reduced duties, but you need certificates of origin. For shipping, use DHL, FedEx, or freight forwarders like Bollore Logistics or Seko Logistics. For small packages under 2kg, registered mail via your post office is cheapest (e.g., Nigeria Post EMS to UK: â¦15,000 for 1kg, 7-14 days). Always include a commercial invoice in a clear plastic pouch on the outside. Mark âCommercial Sampleâ only if true. For returns, customs can be a nightmareâoften cheaper to refund and let customer keep item. Use tools like Zonos or Avalara for duty calculation. Consider using a 3PL in the destination country to avoid customs delays. For African sellers, a common route is to ship to a US address (like a freight forwarder) then reship. Always keep tracking and proof of export. Customs delays of 2-4 weeks are normal. Factor in 15-20% extra for duties and taxes. Never lie on customs formsâit can destroy your business.

lessons.title: Handling Returns and Refunds Efficiently
lessons.body: Returns are part of reselling. In Africa, return rates are lower (2-5%) than in the US (15-30%), but you must have a policy. State clearly: âReturns accepted within 7 days if item is unused and in original packaging. Buyer pays return shipping.â For defective items, you pay return shipping. Use a return authorization (RA) number. For local returns, use a courier like GIG or Pickup Mtaani to pick up from customer. For international, itâs often cheaper to refund without returnâespecially for low-value items. For FBA, Amazon handles returns; you can choose to have items returned to you or disposed. Set up automated refunds in your store (Shopify, WooCommerce) to save time. When a return arrives, inspect within 48 hours. If resellable, restock; if not, claim insurance or write off. Keep a returns log: order ID, reason, action, cost. Analyze reasons: wrong size, damaged, not as described. Fix root causes: better photos, accurate descriptions, stronger packaging. For refunds, use the same payment method. In Nigeria, Paystack and Flutterwave make refunds easy. For cash-on-delivery orders, refund via bank transfer. Always communicate with the customerâa happy return experience can turn a negative into a loyal customer. Offer a discount code on next purchase. Track return rate per product; if a product has >10% returns, stop selling it. Efficient returns management protects your profit and reputation.
